tagline: A leading global wealth manager and systemically important bank strengthened by the integration of Credit Suisse, delivering strong returns and sustainable growth
hero_kpi_rationale: Net profit is the primary performance indicator for a universal bank like UBS, reflecting the successful integration of Credit Suisse and the return-to-profitability trajectory, with net profit of $3.0 billion in Q1 2026.

kpis.name: Net Profit
kpis.explanation: Net profit is what the bank earns after all expenses, including taxes.
kpis.description: Net profit of $3.0 billion in Q1 2026 demonstrates strong financial performance driven by franchise strength and positive client momentum, despite ongoing integration costs. This positions UBS on track to achieve its targeted 15% RoCET1 return by 2026.
kpis.signal: $3.0 billion net profit in Q1 2026, up 80% year-on-year.

kpis.name: CET1 Capital Ratio
kpis.explanation: The CET1 ratio measures a bank's financial strength: the higher it is, the stronger and better capitalized the bank.
kpis.description: A CET1 ratio of 14.7% at the end of Q1 2026 shows UBS is well capitalized, reinforcing investor confidence and enabling dividend distributions while maintaining a significant capital buffer against new Swiss regulatory requirements.
kpis.signal: CET1 at 14.7%, comfortably above the guidance of around 14%.

kpis.name: Cumulative Cost Savings Achieved
kpis.explanation: Cumulative amount of cost savings achieved through the integration of Credit Suisse, progressing toward the total target of $13 billion.
kpis.description: UBS has achieved $11.5 billion in cumulative cost savings by the end of Q1 2026, representing 88% of the total $13 billion target. These savings enable UBS to invest further in talent, technology, and products while progressing toward substantial completion of the integration by end-2026.
kpis.signal: 88% of the $13 billion target already achieved, with an additional $0.8 billion in savings in Q1 2026.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.explanation: Amount paid to each shareholder per share held, with double-digit growth in 2026.
kpis.description: A double-digit dividend increase for 2026 reflects strong results and continued commitment to shareholders, supported by robust capital generation.
kpis.signal: Double-digit dividend growth accumulated by Q1 2026, signaling confidence in the financial trajectory.

kpis.name: Share Repurchase
kpis.explanation: Amount the bank uses to buy back its own shares in the market to support shareholder value.
kpis.description: UBS repurchased $0.9 billion of shares in Q1 2026 and is on track to reach $3 billion in buybacks by Q2 2026 results, with potential for further repurchases by year-end, supporting shareholder value.
kpis.signal: $0.9 billion in repurchases in Q1 2026, on track to deliver $3 billion by Q2 2026 results.

kpis.name: Return on CET1 Capital
kpis.explanation: Measures the return generated on CET1 capital, a key profitability metric for banks.
kpis.description: A return on CET1 capital of 16.8% in Q1 2026 demonstrates exceptional financial performance and strong execution, positioning UBS to exceed its annual 15% target for 2026.
kpis.signal: RoCET1 of 16.8% in Q1 2026, exceeding internal guidance of approximately 15% for 2026.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €1617.43 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €336.04 billion in the latest year

risks.title: Post-acquisition integration of Credit Suisse
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central in the 10-K, mentioned upfront with strong language ("execution risk", "most complex part"). The trend is stable as integration progresses but remains critical. The Competition category is key as integration aims to strengthen positioning against competitors.

risks.title: Increased regulation in Switzerland
risks.score_rationale: Highly positioned in the text, with alarmed language ("ill-informed public debate", "intensified demands"). Trend is rising as political pressures intensify in 2025. The Regulation category is central with direct impact on the business model.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and reliance on generative AI
risks.score_rationale: Explicit mention of AI tools such as Red and Copilot, with language indicating widespread adoption. Trend is rising. The Cybersecurity category is relevant as exposure to digital risks increases with AI usage.

risks.title: Dependence on key technology talent
risks.score_rationale: Mention of strategic hires (e.g. Lila Tretikov, AI expert) and investments in employees. Language emphasizes talent value. Trend is rising. The Key Person category is critical for innovation.

risks.title: Reputational pressures related to the acquisition
risks.score_rationale: Significant presence in the letter, with explicit efforts to differentiate UBS from Credit Suisse. Defensive language. Trend is stable. The Reputation category is central in a context of public distrust.

risks.title: Increased competition in wealth management
risks.score_rationale: Mention of #1 position in Asia Pacific and the Americas, with growth ambitions. Offensive language on market share gains. Trend is stable. The Competition category is strategic.

risks.title: Climate transition-related risks
risks.score_rationale: Mention of decarbonization targets and ESG commitments, but with measured language. Trend is stable. The Environment category is present but secondary compared to operational risks.

ai_positioning.summary: UBS has integrated artificial intelligence as a major strategic component of its digital transformation, with over 500 AI solutions in production and 750 in development across the bank. UBS's AI approach focuses on enhancing customer experience and employee productivity.
evidence: Over 500 AI use cases in production and approximately 750 in development across the organization
